title: A new look for TENET
question: Three branding directions for the whole inspector. Choose one, ask for a revision, or re-roll. These are visual proposals, not implemented screens.

options.label: 01 · Signal desk
options.thesis: A precise measurement instrument for understanding a recorded decision.
options.viewport: A narrow session index beside a large command display, a decisive outcome readout and an exact evidence-confidence scale.
options.risk: Physical-instrument styling can become a costume; the controls must remain ordinary, readable software.

raised.raise: Give the session index enough density to support scanning, rather than wasting its height.
Make selection and disclosure states unmistakable without relying on accent color.
Keep numeric readings exact and the threshold directly adjacent to the measured value.
Make expanded evidence visibly belong to its originating rule.
Use one large, continuous field for the command rather than a collection of little cards.

options.label: 02 · Trace studio
options.thesis: A contemporary tracing workspace with a recognisable plum-and-lilac identity.
options.viewport: A dark call rail frames a broad light-lilac decision workspace, with action, policy and execution expressed as a readable trace.
options.risk: The most familiar developer-tool option; it needs strong composition to avoid becoming another dark sidebar app.

options.label: 03 · Wayfinder
options.thesis: The decision is a sign you can read instantly, with evidence one turn away.
options.viewport: A bold yellow navigation rail meets a black outcome band and a quiet white evidence area.
options.case: Stronger at immediate product clarity; less native to developers than a tracing workspace.
options.risk: Yellow must mean navigation, not a warning; decision status needs its own explicit words and symbols.

options.label: Event catalog
options.thesis: Calls as tightly packed indexed cells.
options.viewport: A grid of commands opens the selected record.
options.risk: Text-heavy calls are harder to inspect in tiny cells.
options.case: Weaker on developer identification and on explaining one decision.

options.label: One-bit desktop
options.viewport: Sessions, rule and evidence appear in tiled windows.
options.risk: Retro chrome competes with long evidence text.
options.case: Nostalgia is less relevant than current debugging habits; the tiled view obscures the decision summary.

options.label: Laboratory counter
options.thesis: Confidence as an exact instrument reading.
options.viewport: A confidence readout dominates the workspace.
options.risk: Overweights the number when the actual outcome matters more.
options.case: Weaker on both developer identification and the distinction between policy and execution.
options.kept: Exact numbers next to their thresholds.

options.label: Transforming textile
options.thesis: Evidence opens as connected folds from a rule.
options.viewport: An expanded evidence region remains attached to its rule.
options.risk: The textile vocabulary adds unfamiliar controls.
options.case: Weaker on both developer identification and immediate explanation.
options.kept: Visible continuity between a rule and its expanded evidence.

options.label: Cloud quarry
options.thesis: Recorded stages as broad stacked layers.
options.viewport: Command, assessment and execution occupy large linked regions.
options.risk: Atmospheric imagery distracts from exact archived facts.
options.case: Weaker on developer identification and product clarity.
options.kept: One continuous command field instead of many competing cards.
